_what: Pluto haze from New Horizons imaging (docs/sources/pluto-haze.md).

gladstone_2016._citation: Gladstone, G. R., Stern, S. A., Ennico, K., et al. (2016). The atmosphere of Pluto as observed by New Horizons. Science 351, aad8866. DOI:10.1126/science.aad8866; text source arXiv:1604.05356v1, section 'Hazes' (p. 8-9).
gladstone_2016._quote: Extensive, optically thin hazes are seen in New Horizons images of Pluto (Fig. 4), extending to altitudes >200 km, with typical brightness scale heights of ~50 km. ... The haze scale height decreases to ~30 km at altitudes 100-200 km ... I/F ... values of ~0.2-0.3 at red wavelengths (in MVIC red, 540-700 nm, and LORRI images, 350-850 nm), and I/F values up to 0.7-0.8 at blue wavelengths (in MVIC blue images, 400-550 nm) ... (e.g., at I/F ~ 0.02 at Theta~38 deg, in MVIC red and blue images), and are just barely detectable at low phase angles (e.g., at I/F ~ 0.003 at Theta~20 deg, in LORRI images) ... with optical constants of n=1.69 and k=0.018 ... at the LORRI pivot wavelength of 607.6 nm ... For optically thin conditions, I/F ~ P(Theta) tau_LOS / 4 ... particles with radii no smaller than ~0.2 um, P(165 deg)~5, leading to tau_LOS ~ 0.16, or a vertical haze scattering optical depth of ~0.013.

cheng_2017._citation: Cheng, A. F., Summers, M. E., Gladstone, G. R., et al. (2017). Haze in Pluto's atmosphere. Icarus 290, 112-133. DOI:10.1016/j.icarus.2017.02.024; text source arXiv:1702.07771v2, Table 4 'Phase Functions of Pluto Haze Particles' (p. 22) and section 5.
cheng_2017._quote: The phase function of Pluto's atmospheric haze at the visible wavelengths observed by LORRI (pivot wavelength 607.6nm) is compiled in Table 4.
cheng_2017._section5_quote: From (1), the line-of-sight scattering optical depth would be ~0.24, and the vertical optical depth would be ~0.018. (section 5, same Mie particles as Gladstone et al.)
